prompt:
Use the attached ORIGINAL ASHVEIL cinder-bear atlas ONLY to keep the same bear identity, anatomy, ash-flecked soot-brown/charcoal fur palette, detailed crisp pixel clusters and camera. Generate a NEW WALK atlas; do not reuse or relabel any of its idle poses. A very heavy 340kg grizzly-like quadruped, round ears, short broad muzzle, massive shoulder hump and rump, four stout jointed legs, broad clawed paws, tiny stub tail. Never a dog/wolf, humanoid, extra head or extra limb. No gear, magic, glowing marks, fire, motion-blur or motion trails.

One square transparent RGBA PNG sprite atlas, EXACTLY 4 ROWS x 4 COLUMNS, 16 separated complete bears. Each row is one direction in this EXACT order: row1 FRONT, head facing down toward viewer; row2 LEFT, nose pointing to left edge and rump at right; row3 RIGHT, nose to right edge and rump at left; row4 BACK, head facing up away from viewer, rump/tiny tail toward viewer. Elevated 3/4 game camera throughout, no side-view switch in front/back rows. No scenery, no text or labels, no grid, no floor, no contact shadow, no checkered background. All remaining pixels transparent. Equal spacing with VERY GENEROUS gutters: each whole bear occupies only the CENTRAL 60 PERCENT of its cell, at least 45px entirely empty margin from any cell boundary in a 1024x1024 atlas. Absolutely no silhouette touches a neighbor or outer canvas edge. Keep head size and overall body mass consistent, do not enlarge side-view bears to fill their cells.

WALK: each row's four columns are FOUR visibly DISTINCT consecutive key poses of one slow weighty four-beat walking loop. 1 near forepaw extended and planted / opposite hind paw preparing; 2 body weight rolls forward, previously extended forepaw under shoulder and other forepaw lifts; 3 opposite forepaw extended and planted, hind legs exchange; 4 opposite passing/support pose returning into frame1. Make forepaws and hindpaws visibly change positions in every column, with believable four-legged support and heavy downward shoulder weight. Keep feet clear and a steady local ground baseline; minimal body bob, no fast running/trotting, no airborne bear, no stretching the body. Front and back rows must also show alternating paws, not four identical still bears. High-quality clean original game art with rich ash-fur detail and readable limbs.
